A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IR-Agent research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures and prompts, support reliable comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on NIST IR spectra, including accuracy comparisons, agent ablations, sensitivity analyses and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds baseline comparisons, robustness tests, runtime measurements and single-compound versus mixture results.

M1.justification: The translator, TI/Ret/SE expert pipeline, training objective, retrieval procedure and substantive prompt instructions remain unchanged. Expanded translator explanations and the ReAct comparator do not establish a modification to the proposed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds an evaluated incomplete-information scenario using carbon-count ranges rather than exact counts (Appendix C.4). The 9,052-spectrum NIST dataset remains; newly documented phase diversity and mixture composition describe retained data rather than a new dataset.

E2.justification: V2 substantially broadens comparison beyond the retained translator and agent variants by evaluating the Patch-Based Self-Attention Transformer, a GPT-4o ReAct workflow, and zero-shot/QLoRA Llama attempts. The Llama version is inconsistently named Llama-3-8B in prose and LLaMA-3.1-8B in Table 6.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols add MACCS/RDKit/Morgan Tanimoto similarity, two paraphrased prompt sets, carbon-count ranges, zero-shot versus QLoRA Llama evaluation, and a ReAct comparison capped at five tool calls. These substantially expand evaluation design; the existing 80/10/10 split and core training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds prompt robustness, ambiguous-information robustness, ReAct tool-selection failure analysis, single-compound/mixture analysis and a new TI reasoning case study (Figure 4; Appendix C.3–C.6). Existing expert ablations, candidate-count sensitivity, beam-width tests and earlier case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages across three independent experiments and parenthesized uncertainty values. Additional accuracy tables follow the existing practice; no changed run counts, new seed information, confidence intervals or formal significance tests are specified.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, but v2 adds substantial new findings. Table 6 reports patch-attention versus IR-Agent Top-1 accuracy of 0.129 versus 0.103 and Top-10 accuracy of 0.181 versus 0.216. Table 10 reveals zero exact-match accuracy for 20 mixture test cases. Robustness, ReAct, similarity and runtime results are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, including the agent definitions, absorbance conversion, positional embeddings and cross-entropy objective, retain their mathematical substance. V2 adds explanatory motivation rather than new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: expert-inspired multi-agent IR structure elucidation, complementary expert reasoning, improved baseline performance and flexible incorporation of chemical information.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations and applicability boundaries concerning mixture failures, latency constraints, dependence on translator quality and ReAct tool-selection failures. These extend v1's limitations concerning peak shapes/intensities and translator retraining, and qualify the framework's practical scope.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset composition/filtering details, pretrained-translator input encoding, measured runtimes and setup information for new comparisons. Core hyperparameters, hardware, software versions, prompt templates and the code link remain. V1's explicit 790k simulated-pretraining sample count is no longer stated.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on IR-only reinforcement learning, Llama and mass-spectrometry/formula inference, removes the shift-robust molecular-learning citation, and more explicitly contrasts its setting with formula-conditioned IR models. The central novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify related work, the task and translator roles. V2 adds a dataset appendix and reproducibility statement, moves Broader Impacts into an Ethics Statement, and updates author/header and citation formatting. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the displays with a new TI case-study figure, five new results tables and timing rows in Table 5. It also revises Figure 1 and adopts conference formatting. The earlier beam-width and supplementary case-study figures are retained as Figures 5–6, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's narrow comparative validation through external-model and ReAct comparisons, robustness tests and clearer applicability evidence (Tables 6–10). Reporting the patch-attention baseline's Top-1 advantage and complete mixture exact-match failure makes the paper more informative and balanced. Added dataset and latency documentation further strengthens assessment, although Llama naming and some new baseline implementation details remain unclear.
